subtopic: The Modulus and the Conjugate of a Complex Number
title: The modulus: distance from the origin

board_content.text: The modulus is the straight-line distance from the origin to $(a,b)$ — Pythagoras on the grid.
$|z|$ is always non-negative — you cannot write $|z|=\pm z$.
Modulus is multiplicative — take it factor by factor across products, powers, quotients.
Each coordinate is at most the whole distance — obvious from the right triangle.

segments_english.text: The conjugate is a reflection; the modulus is a distance. Together they run the whole chapter.
The modulus of z is the square root of a squared plus b squared, and it is always greater than or equal to zero.

Geometrically it's the straight-line distance from the origin to the point a comma b. If the address tells you how to walk there, the modulus tells you how far it is, as the crow flies. It's just Pythagoras on the grid.

A crucial warning: the modulus is always non-negative. The real-number habit of writing absolute value equals plus or minus x does not carry over. You can never write modulus of z equals plus or minus z.

The properties are clean. The modulus of z equals the modulus of its conjugate equals the modulus of minus z. The modulus of a product is the product of moduli, and the modulus of a power is the power of the modulus.
So modulus is multiplicative. For any product, power, or quotient, take the modulus factor by factor instead of multiplying everything out first.
Two more bounds: the size of the real part is at most the modulus, and the size of the imaginary part is at most the modulus.
That's obvious once you picture the right triangle: neither leg can be longer than the hypotenuse, which is the modulus.

segments_hinglish.text: Conjugate ek reflection hai; modulus ek distance hai. Dono milke poora chapter chalate hain.
z ka modulus hai a square plus b square ka square root, aur ye hamesha zero se greater than or equal to hota hai.

Geometrically ye origin se point a comma b tak ki straight-line distance hai. Agar address batata hai wahan kaise chalna hai, to modulus batata hai kitna door hai, as the crow flies. Ye bas grid par Pythagoras hai.

Ek crucial warning: modulus hamesha non-negative hai. Real-number wali aadat, absolute value barabar plus or minus x likhne ki, yahan nahi chalti. Aap kabhi modulus of z barabar plus or minus z nahi likh sakte.
Properties clean hain. z ka modulus barabar uske conjugate ka modulus barabar minus z ka modulus. Product ka modulus hai moduli ka product, aur power ka modulus hai modulus ki power.
To modulus multiplicative hai. Kisi bhi product, power, ya quotient ke liye, sab kuch expand karne ke bajaay modulus ko factor by factor lo.
Do aur bounds: real part ka size at most modulus hai, aur imaginary part ka size at most modulus hai.
Ye obvious hai jab aap right triangle picture karo: koi bhi leg hypotenuse se lambi nahi ho sakti, jo hai modulus.
